plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of beliefs about others' bids or the number of competitors. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win at a high second price; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since truthful bidding maximizes expected profit against any rational opponents, I will bid exactly my value: $27.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (given you win). Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying relative to value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of competitors' strategies, the optimal action is straightforward truthful bidding. My value is $31, so I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you bid your true value, you win whenever the highest competing bid is below your value, and win only when it's profitable (since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid). This holds even if others deviate from truthful bidding. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $20.
